verdict: Creating and inspecting drop links is well covered - settings accordion, budgets, the per-session event log. The weak spot is the settings save: it re-renders the whole view the moment the request returns, so both the 'Saved'/'failed' message and any edits vanish, and every save quietly moves the expiry date. The detail page also knows far less than the app does (no per-link chart, no link to the share of this folder, history silently capped at 200).

findings.title: Do not re-render the detail view on top of a failed save
findings.scenario: Admin edits five fields in Settings and clicks Save; the PATCH fails (network, 500) or succeeds.
findings.consequence: saveDetail() writes 'Save failed.' and then immediately calls refreshDetail(), whose renderDetail() replaces #detail-view including #detail-msg - the message disappears within a few hundred ms and, on failure, every edited field snaps back to the server value, so the admin's changes are lost without a visible error.
findings.fix: On !r.ok, show the server's error text (await r.json().error) and return without refreshDetail(). On success, call refreshDetail() first and set #detail-msg ('Saved.') after it resolves; use a success class instead of msg-err.

findings.title: Only send expiresDays when the admin changed it
findings.scenario: A link expires in 2 days 3 hours; the admin opens Settings to change the label and saves.
findings.consequence: The form shows Math.ceil(remaining) = 3 and saveDetail always sends expiresDays, so patchLink sets expiresAt = now + 3 days: every unrelated save silently extends the link by up to a day, and a link can be kept alive indefinitely by editing it.
findings.fix: Remember the rendered d-days value and include expiresDays in the PATCH body only if the input differs from it (same pattern as the pin field).

findings.title: Say when upload history is truncated
findings.scenario: A link has received 1,204 files; recent:<slug> holds only the newest 200 (RECENT_CAP).
findings.consequence: The Files card says 1,204 while the history header says '200 files · 38 GB' with no hint that the list is capped; searching for an older file returns 'No files match the filter' although it exists.
findings.fix: When uploads.length < link.stats.files, render '200 most recent of 1,204 - sync from Drive for all' in #up-count and make the empty-filter message offer the Drive sync.

findings.title: Surface failures from pause, archive and delete
findings.scenario: The admin session expired, or KV rejects the write, and the admin clicks Pause on a link being abused.
findings.consequence: The fetch result is ignored; refreshAll() redraws the card unchanged and the admin believes the link is paused when it is not.
findings.fix: Check r.ok in toggleLinkPause/toggleLinkArchive/deleteLink and flash the returned error on the clicked button (flash() already exists in admin.js).

missing_features.title: Per-link 30-day chart on the detail page
missing_features.why: 'When did people actually upload to this link?' has no answer on the page that is about this link.
missing_features.where: Link detail, under the stat cards

missing_features.title: Share this drop's folder from the detail page
missing_features.why: The 'share this folder' shortcut only exists on the create-success screen; a week later the admin has to rebuild it by hand in the Shares tab.

missing_features.title: Extend / set expiry as an explicit action
missing_features.why: Expiry is a 'days from now' number buried in the Access accordion; the common task is 'give them one more week'.
missing_features.where: Link detail header next to the status chip

interlinks.to: the share link(s) whose folderIds include this drop's folderId
interlinks.why: shows at once whether the uploaders' files have been shared back

interlinks.from: Top uploaders row / Upload history uploader cell
interlinks.why: one click from a name to everything that person did

interlinks.to: System log filtered to that session id
interlinks.why: server-side errors for the same session are in the Logs tab

layout: Move 'Upload sessions' (debug) below Settings - it is a troubleshooting tool, and on a healthy link it pushes the settings far down the page.
Show the budget bar inside the stat grid's 'Received' card instead of as a separate strip under it.
